correctness.rationale: For unweighted adjacency on the Cartesian power H(d,q)=K_q^{square d}, exp(itA) factorizes into d coordinate unitaries. The one-coordinate probability matrix has constant-eigenspace eigenvalue 1 and perpendicular-eigenspace eigenvalue a(t)=(q-2+2cos(qt))/q. Tensor diagonalization gives a(t)^j with multiplicity binom(d,j)(q-1)^j. Its common-period average equals q^{-j}[z^0](q-2+z+z^{-1})^j, and expansion yields the stated nonnegative sum. q>=3 has positive constant-term contribution (q-2)^j; q=2 has zero exactly at odd j and positive binom(2a,a)/4^a at j=2a. The binomial-multiplicity sum gives rank q^d or 2^(d-1), including d=1. Independently counted equal-weight character pairs for 36 (q,d,j) cases with 2<=q<=5 and 1<=d<=3; this checks normalization but the tensor argument proves all dimensions. The q-alphabet need not be a field.
